consolidated.eventCardPolicy: One rule for all 48 'Trips We Plan Often' event-cards (4 per experience page x 12). (1) PRIMARY CTA never moves. .event-cta keeps its label ('Plan This Trip' / 'Request X Package') and its target, /plan-your-trip/. Where the experience maps cleanly to a supported form type, append the prefill: beach-island-escapes and all-inclusive-vacations -> ?type=beach; family-travel -> ?type=family; multigenerational-travel -> ?type=group; cruises -> ?type=cruise; safari-wildlife-travel -> ?type=safari; romance 'The Honeymoon, Full Stop' -> ?type=honeymoon; romance 'The Birthday Worth the Flight' -> ?type=group. Every other card (adventure, culture, food-wine, sports, wellness, and the romance anniversary/proposal cards) keeps the bare URL. The form's canonical strips the query, so this creates no duplicate URLs. Verify the form actually reads ?type= before shipping. (2) Each card may carry AT MOST ONE secondary text link, placed in .event-body under the CTA (the .event-card is a div; nestedCardAnchors guards only .exp-card and .place-card, so confirm that selector before the first one ships). It is styled by one shared class in experience.css (no pageCss) and phrased as '<Place> in detail →'. Its target is always the SAME canonical page as the card's subject (see subjects), choosing the deepest stable section that honestly matches, in this order: #itineraries when that page's Trips We Plan Often section carries the same or a closely matching itinerary; else #places when a place-card is the closest match; else a named section id on an approved new page; else the page root. (3) A secondary link ships only when the target text already supports the card. If an enhancement is pending (Inca Trail -> Peru, Riviera Maya Family Week, Portugal Three-Generation, Burgundy -> France, Sri Lanka Ayurveda, Japan onsen towns) or a new page is pending (Dolomites, St. Lucia, tennis #wimbledon, formula-1 #monaco, mediterranean #dalmatian-coast, european-river-cruises #rhone, yacht-charters #gulets), the card ships with no secondary link, or with the named interim, until the target exists. (4) Card copy that contradicts its target page is fixed before the link goes live: Seychelles flights/Beau Vallon/season, St. Barth's season, Sri Lanka season and the 'under three hours' claim, Bali May-October, Tulum November-April, Japan Sunrise Seto routing and Beppu/Dogo claims, Peru acclimatization (Sacred Valley first), Patagonia dates, Cape Town 'guaranteed Big Five' and season, Costa Rica beach half, and renaming the 'Riviera Maya Adults Escape' collision. (5) Never mark event-cards up as Offer, TouristTrip or Event. (6) Anchor convention: id=\"itineraries\" on section.itineraries-section in ONE pass across every destination partial that has the section (Maldives has none; use the page root). This rejects id=\"trips\". Ship it with a card-fragment-resolves verifier check plus fixtures that go red, because the dead-link check strips fragments and would pass a missing id. EXCEPTIONS: the romance anniversary, proposal and birthday cards get no secondary link (the occasion is the product, and any destination would pre-empt it). The Masters card links the existing journal explainer (/travel-journal/masters-field-report/) because that is the subject's canonical. Alpine Ski Season links the heli-ski report labelled for the heli option only. Antarctica, Done Properly links /destinations/antarctica/#itineraries, not the polar hub. The Maldives Overwater Classic links the Maldives page root (no itineraries section). Multigenerational Italy (family-travel) links /destinations/italy/#itineraries rather than the multigenerational experience page. Jamaica Couples Week, Tulum Jungle Digital Detox, Sri Lanka Ayurvedic Immersion and Japan Onsen & Ryokan Circuit use #places because no matching itinerary exists.

verdicts.reasoning: Reusing /destinations/peru/ is right. The page already delivers most of what the three tiles promise: the 500/day cap and Sun Gate arrival (FAQ 3 'Inca Trail vs train'), altitude, season, and Lima food (the Lima place-card plus FAQ 4 naming Astrid y Gaston, La Mar and Isolina). The gaps are the ones the spec names. All four itin-cards go by train or bus. Salkantay/Lares, Central and Surquillo are absent, though the food tile (food-wine-travel exp-card 7) leads with 'Virgilio Martinez's Central' and 'market stalls in Surquillo'. The spec has four defects. (1) The proposed trek itinerary goes Lima, 2 Sacred Valley nights, then the trail, skipping Cusco. briefs.answerCapsuleDirection: 40–70 words under the intro h2, answering "Disney, Universal, or both, and for how long?" Shape: Disney World has 4 theme parks and suits kids from about age 4. Universal has 3 theme parks since Epic Universe opened on May 22, 2025, and its headline rides need 40–48 inches, so it fits roughly 8 and up. A week split 4 Disney days, 2 Universal days and 1 pool day covers both. Sources for every number: park counts and the Epic Universe opening date come from disneyworld.disney.go.com and universalorlando.com (newsroom); the 40/48-inch heights from Universal's ride-height-requirements page (already linked on family-travel); "age 4" and "under-3s free" from Disney's ticket page. The 4/2/1 split is HYMT's recommendation and must be phrased as advice, not a statistic. Put a dated "Checked <Month> 2026" note nearby, since Typhoon Lagoon and Lightning Lane pricing are perishable.

briefs.primaryIntent: A single-island St. Lucia week. The page answers which side of the island to base on (Soufrière under the Pitons, or the north: Rodney Bay, Cap Estate, Castries), whether a boutique sanctuary beats an all-inclusive here, how a honeymoon is shaped, and what the transfer from Hewanorra (UVF) means for flight choice and resort choice. The Barbados + St. Lucia two-island trip stays on /destinations/barbados-eastern-caribbean/.
briefs.workingTitle: St. Lucia: Pitons, Soufrière or the North — Hit Your Mark Travel (64 chars incl. suffix; fallback "St. Lucia: Soufrière vs the North — Hit Your Mark Travel", 56 chars)
briefs.h1Direction:
Use the hero headline as the single H1, the same way Turks & Caicos uses "The Best Beach in the Western Hemisphere Is Here." It should state the deciding fact, not use the brand or a label. Direction: the Pitons decide the view, and the airport decides the base. Example shape: "Two Pitons, Two Airports,
One Decision About Where to Sleep." Keep it under 70 characters with tags stripped. The hero sub (2–3 sentences) says plainly that the island is about 27 miles long (source: Government of Saint Lucia or CIA World Factbook), that long-haul flights land at Hewanorra in the far south, and that Soufrière and the north are two different holidays.
briefs.metaDescription: Soufrière or the north, boutique or all-inclusive, and the long road from Hewanorra: planning a St. Lucia week under the Pitons, December to April.

sections: 1. <section class="intro-section">: h2.intro-title as a statement (e.g. 'The Pitons Are in the South. So Is the Airport.'), then p.answer-capsule, then 2–3 p.intro-body. Body: Soufrière vs the north, and the boutique-vs-all-inclusive split. Name the Barbados pairing in prose with a link to /destinations/barbados-eastern-caribbean/ ('pairing St. Lucia with Barbados'), so that two-island product stays there. intro-image--photo uses a NEW portrait np- image (see imageGaps), not np-e-44, which Barbados already uses as its intro.

2. <section class="places-section" id="places"> with places-grid places-grid--even places-grid--photo. Four or six place-cards, one per real base or area: Soufrière & the Pitons (Gros/Petit Piton, UNESCO Pitons Management Area 2004, Sulphur Springs); Anse Chastanet / Anse Mamin coast (reef, the Jade Mountain/Anse Chastanet pairing already named in the journal guide); Rodney Bay & Pigeon Island (north, Pigeon Island National Landmark); Cap Estate / the far north (all-inclusive and golf base); optionally Marigot Bay and the rainforest interior / Edmund Forest Reserve. Each card is an <a class="place-card"> with no inner <a>, and each needs a distinct real photo. The photo gate blocks shipping six cards until six photos exist. Ship four if only four are real.

3. <section class="itineraries-section"> 'Trips We Plan Often': 3–4 itin-cards with itin-image--photo portraits. (a) Soufrière Honeymoon Week, 7 days; (b) St. Lucia All-Inclusive Week, north base, 7 days, built from the all-inclusive event-card 4 copy, with its duration line set to 'December – April · 5–7 Days' and May named as shoulder in the season block; (c) Split stay, north then Soufrière, 8–9 days; (d) optional Active week: Gros Piton climb, rainforest, diving. No Barbados+St. Lucia card. Point to it instead in prose or the related grid.

4. <section class="why-section"> 'What We Add to St. Lucia Planning': 4 why-items. UVF vs GFL (George F. L. Charles) arrival and transfer by road, boat or helicopter. Choosing between Soufrière's open-wall/view properties and beachfront. All-inclusive vs boutique, and which properties are adults-only. Booking lead time for Dec–Apr Pitons-view rooms (NEEDS MARK for his lead-time figure).

5. <section class="seasons-strip"> 'St. Lucia by Season': season-item--best Dry Season December – April; Shoulder May–June & November; Hurricane/Wet Season June–November, with the peak months cited to NOAA/NHC. St. Lucia Jazz & Arts Festival (May) and Carnival (July) only if verified with stlucia.org and dated.
6. NEEDS MARK testimonial comment placeholder, as on Turks & Caicos. No invented quote.
7. <section class="dest-cta"> with h2.dest-cta__title 'Plan a St. Lucia Trip…', btn-primary-gold -> /plan-your-trip/, btn-ghost-gold -> /destinations/caribbean-mexico/.

8. <section class="related-section"> 'Destinations Worth Comparing': related-cards to /destinations/barbados-eastern-caribbean/ (described as the two-island pairing), /destinations/st-barths/, /destinations/turks-caicos/ (the hub's other two honeymoon picks) and optionally /destinations/jamaica/ (the all-inclusive comparison). rc- crops already exist for those pages.

9. <section class="cost-range"> 'What St. Lucia Actually Costs': per-person per-day range split boutique vs all-inclusive, what moves it (Pitons-view category, Dec 20–Jan 5 holiday minimums, transfer mode), and a dated 'verified as of' line. NEEDS FIGURE until Mark supplies or confirms the ranges.

11. <section class="read-more"> 'Read More on St. Lucia': read-more__cards to /travel-journal/caribbean-mexico-destination-guide/ (it already covers Jade Mountain and Soufrière), /travel-journal/what-hotel-descriptions-actually-mean/ (resort-marketing vs reality, all-inclusive), and /travel-journal/the-case-for-shoulder-season/ (May/June). That gives at least 2 journal links to satisfy internal-link-floor.
briefs.answerCapsuleDirection: 40–70 words directly under the intro h2. Cover: the dry season runs December–April with May as shoulder, which matches the hero stat and the Barbados and Turks capsules. A week is the norm, 7 nights. The base decision is Soufrière (the Pitons, boutique, view-led) vs the north (Rodney Bay/Cap Estate, beaches, most all-inclusives). Long-haul flights land at Hewanorra (UVF) in the south. Source for each number: dry-season months from the Saint Lucia Meteorological Services climate normals or NOAA/NHC hurricane-season dates (June 1–Nov 30); the UVF-to-Soufrière and UVF-to-Rodney Bay road times only from the Saint Lucia Tourism Authority (stlucia.org) or SLASPA airport guidance, else NEEDS FIGURE (never estimate a transfer time); trip length from Mark's own booking pattern (NEEDS MARK if he hasn't stated one; Barbados's capsule uses '7–8 days' as a single-island week and can be mirrored only if Mark confirms). Do not put the UNESCO 2004 date in the capsule. It belongs on the place-card.

briefs.name: Tennis (Wimbledon, Roland Garros, Australian Open)
briefs.template: ExperienceLayout, nested at src/pages/experiences/sports-event-travel/tennis/index.astro with content in src/content-pages/experiences__sports-event-travel__tennis.html. It needs the new optional parent prop described in rules-data-template-qa.md section 11. Use section 11's prop shape, parent?: { label: string; href: string }, not the {name, path} the verifier text uses, so the plan has one spec. Pass parent={{ label: "Sports & Event Travel", href: "/experiences/sports-event-travel/" }}, name="Tennis", schemaType="website". Hero image: /assets/img/e-23-wimbledon-pimms.jpg, which is currently unused in src. Pass it as preloadImage through the hero, the same way the layout does today. Hero ctaSecondary should be "Compare the routes ↓", pointing at #wimbledon. Use only the existing experience.css classes. No pageCss, no new CSS.
briefs.primaryIntent: Commercial-investigation intent for Grand Slam access: how to actually get a seat at Wimbledon, and what it costs. The page compares debenture vs official hospitality vs the public ballot and the Queue, with lead times. It then gives the Roland Garros and Australian Open equivalents, plus dates and where to stay. The page earns its place through the side-by-side comparison across all three routes and all three tournaments. The AELTC, FFT and Tennis Australia sites each describe only their own products and never compare across tournaments. It is not a narrative explainer.
briefs.workingTitle: Wimbledon & Grand Slam Tennis Travel — Hit Your Mark Travel
briefs.h1Direction:
The H1 is the hero headline, which the layout renders. Make it a short promise built around the seat decision, not "luxury tennis". For example: "Centre Court, Philippe-Chatrier, Rod Laver Arena", or "Three Slams, Three Ways In". Keep it to one h1, written in the existing
two-line style. The eyebrow is "Sports & Event Travel · Tennis". The hero sub must name the three routes: debenture, official hospitality, ballot.
briefs.metaDescription: Wimbledon debenture, official hospitality or the ballot? The three routes compared, plus Roland Garros (late May) and the Australian Open (January).
briefs.breadcrumb: Home > Experiences > Sports & Event Travel > Tennis. Both the visible trail and the BreadcrumbList are rendered from the same trail array once the parent prop lands, and the parent crumb links to /experiences/sports-event-travel/. A page under /experiences/<parent>/<child>/ that emits only 3 crumbs must fail the build. That needs a verifier fixture in tools/verify-checks.test.mjs.
briefs.schemaNodes: WebPage + BreadcrumbList (4 items: Home, Experiences, Sports & Event Travel, Tennis) + Service (name and serviceType "Tennis", provider = Organization @id, description = meta description) + FAQPage, extracted automatically from the page-faq block by extractFaq. Nothing else. No AggregateRating, and no SportsEvent/Event nodes: HYMT does not sell the tickets, and per-year event markup would go stale. Do not chase FAQ rich results. The FAQPage node is emitted only because the layout emits it.
sections: 1. intro-section. label 'Why Tennis Travel'. First h2, for example 'Three Grand Slams, Three Different Ways In', then the p.answer-capsule, then 2-3 intro-body paragraphs. The required 'who this is for / who it is not for' paragraph goes here as an intro-body paragraph, because no experience page has a dedicated class for it. Not for: anyone who wants a guaranteed seat on a specific court on a specific day for under the debenture-resale price, or anyone unwilling to commit to dates 6-12 months out. Use the intro-image--photo portrait slot. This is a gap: no np- tennis portrait exists.

2. exp-cards-section, id="wimbledon". This is THE comparison section, and its id is what the parent's #wimbledon deep link targets. h2 like 'Wimbledon: Debenture vs Hospitality vs Ballot'. The comparison goes in a plain <table> inside the section (rows: route, what you get, which courts, how sold, typical lead time, transferable?, source). Columns: Centre Court debenture; No.1 Court debenture; Official Hospitality (AELTC-appointed caterer packages); the AELTC Public Ballot; the Queue; Ticketmaster/official resale. Every figure is cited to AELTC (wimbledon.com tickets, debentures pages) or the Wimbledon Debenture Holders' official ticket exchange. No exp-card grid with <a> children: if cards are used, they are whole-card anchors with no nested links, and each needs a real photo under exp-cards--photo. Prefer the table plus 3 short intro-body notes.

3. Second content block, id="roland-garros". Reuse exp-cards-section, or an events-section block with one event-card. h2 like 'Roland Garros: Loges, Hospitality and the Public Sale'. Comparison table of FFT box/loge and official hospitality vs the public ticket release vs official resale, with dates, citing FFT/rolandgarros.com. One sentence plus a link to /destinations/france/#places (Paris card) for where to stay. Visible link text: 'planning Paris around the fortnight'.

4. Third block, id="australian-open". h2 like 'Australian Open: Rod Laver Arena Packages and Ground Passes'. Table of Tennis Australia official premium/hospitality vs reserved seating vs ground pass, citing ausopen.com / Tennis Australia. Link /destinations/australia/#places (Melbourne & the Great Ocean Road card), anchor text like 'Melbourne before or after the Open'.

5. events-section 'Trips We Plan Often'. 3 event-cards using the existing event-when/event-name/event-desc/event-meta/event-cta markup. (a) Wimbledon fortnight + London: CTA /plan-your-trip/, body links to /destinations/uk-ireland/#places. (b) Roland Garros + Paris/Champagne. (c) Australian Open + Melbourne/Great Ocean Road. Each package description carries a NEEDS MARK, and each needs a real ev- 3:4 photo. Only ev-e-27-wimbledon-pimms-terrace exists, and the parent already uses it. Generate ev- crops for Paris and Melbourne, or drop to an events grid with a photo on every card.

6. inclusions-section 'What We Handle Around the Seat'. 4 inclusion-items: hotel within reach of SW19 / Porte d'Auteuil / Melbourne Park, transfers vs the District line / Metro / tram (cite TfL and PTV for travel times), dining, and rest days between sessions. The copy must not repeat the parent's generic four inclusions word for word.

7. seasons-strip 'The Grand Slam Calendar'. season-items: January Melbourne (Australian Open, 2 weeks), late May to early June Paris (Roland Garros), late June to July London (Wimbledon), and optionally late August to September New York (US Open), as a mention only with no section. Mark the next edition's season-item--best only if dates are confirmed. Each date comes from the governing body's published calendar, with the 'checked on' date shown on the page.
8. exp-cta. Same pattern as the parent: 'Plan My Trip' to /plan-your-trip/, ghost button back to /experiences/sports-event-travel/ ('All sports and events').

9. cost-range, inserted the same way as tools/p3-8-cost-insert.mjs. Basis: priced by the seat per day, as on the parent. Figures only from AELTC (published debenture prices), FFT or Tennis Australia published package prices, with a dated source line. If no published price is found, use cost-range__figure--unit wording and a NEEDS FIGURE comment, never an estimate.

10. page-faq. 6-10 items in the exact pf-item / h3.pf-q-h / button.pf-q / div.pf-a role=region markup, with ids pf-tennis-1..n. The first sentence of each answer must be a complete answer of 25 words or fewer.

11. read-more. At least 2 journal links, which the verifier requires. masters-field-report: 'how access to a sold-out event actually works', the closest analogue to debentures. what-a-travel-advisor-actually-does: what an advisor can and cannot get you. The third should be europe-destination-guide, or the-case-for-shoulder-season, framed as staying on after the fortnight. Avoid the kentucky-derby report unless it is the only fit.
briefs.answerCapsuleDirection: 40-70 words directly under the first h2. Answer: 'How do you actually get good seats at Wimbledon, Roland Garros and the Australian Open?' Name the three routes in one sentence: a debenture seat, official hospitality, or the public ballot or sale. State the one fact that separates them, for example that a Wimbledon debenture is the only transferable Centre Court ticket. Include at least one number, all taken from AELTC pages: the number of Centre Court debentures in an issue, the 5-year debenture term, or when the ballot opens and closes. Do not use the parent's '6-18 months' figure unless an authority supports it for tennis. If the number cannot be verified from AELTC, FFT or Tennis Australia at writing time, leave a NEEDS FIGURE comment rather than a guessed number. No adjectives in place of facts.
faqCandidates: What is a Wimbledon debenture, and can a visitor buy a single day's seat? (AELTC; Debenture Holders' official exchange)
How does the Wimbledon public ballot work, and when does it open? (AELTC ballot page, with dates shown on the page)
Is the Wimbledon Queue realistic for show-court seats? (AELTC Guide to Queueing)
What is the difference between Wimbledon Official Hospitality and buying a debenture seat? (AELTC hospitality page)
Are resale or secondary-market Wimbledon tickets valid? (AELTC conditions of sale, which say tickets are non-transferable except debentures)

When are Roland Garros and the Australian Open, and which week is best to attend? (FFT / Tennis Australia calendars; first week = more matches across courts, second week = marquee matches; cite the order of play structure)
How do Roland Garros hospitality and public tickets go on sale? (FFT)
Where should I stay for Wimbledon, Roland Garros or the Australian Open? (Answer with distance or transit facts from TfL / RATP / PTV; NEEDS MARK for hotel preferences)
Is there a dress code at Wimbledon? (AELTC: none for spectators except in some hospitality and debenture areas; verify)
Can I combine a Grand Slam with a wider trip? (Answer briefly, then link uk-ireland, france, australia)
authoritativeSources: AELTC / wimbledon.com: tickets overview, Public Ballot, Guide to Queueing, Debentures (current issue, term, number of seats), Official Hospitality, Conditions of Sale, Championships dates
The All England Lawn Tennis Ground plc debenture issue documents (prospectus) for the term and price of the current series
Wimbledon Debenture Holders' official ticket exchange: how debenture seats are legitimately resold
FFT / rolandgarros.com: ticketing calendar, Official Hospitality and Loges, official resale, tournament dates
Tennis Australia / ausopen.com: ticket on-sale dates, Rod Laver Arena / Marvel Arena seating, premium and hospitality packages, Ground Pass, dates
Transport for London (Southfields / Wimbledon stations), RATP (Porte d'Auteuil), Public Transport Victoria (Melbourne Park trams): travel-time facts
ATP/WTA calendars only to confirm the Slam order. The governing bodies above remain the primary source for dates

briefs.primaryIntent: Commercial-investigational. The visitor has settled on a private, whole-boat crewed charter rather than a cabin on someone else's ship, and wants to know how it works before they enquire: which boat type (Turkish gulet, sailing or power catamaran, motor yacht), what the crew does, how the contract and the APA (Advance Provisioning Allowance) work, how the week is priced, and which cruising ground suits which month. The page serves cruises exp-card 6 "Private Yacht Charters" (Turkish gulets, Greek catamarans, Caribbean motor yachts, crew and chef) and, through #gulets, cruises event-card 4 "A Gulet of Your Own" (7-day crewed gulet on the Turquoise Coast). It does not cover shared small-ship or cabin cruising, which belongs to the parent and to /experiences/cruises/mediterranean/.
briefs.workingTitle: Private Crewed Yacht Charters — Hit Your Mark Travel
briefs.h1Direction:
The H1 is the hero headline that ExperienceLayout renders, and it is the only H1. Name the format and the ownership, e.g. "Your Boat, Your Crew,
Your Anchorages". Do not reuse the parent's "The Right Ship Changes Everything". The hero sub, in one or two sentences, names the three vessel types (gulet, catamaran, motor yacht), says the whole boat and crew are yours for the week, and names the two grounds (the Mediterranean and the Caribbean). No superlatives.
briefs.metaDescription: Crewed gulets, catamarans and motor yachts, chartered by the week in the Med or the Caribbean: how crew, contract and the APA work, and what moves the price.

The visible trail and the BreadcrumbList render from the same trail array, so they match by construction. Every crumb is a link except the last, which is the current page.

All four are emitted by ExperienceLayout and required by schema-required on the /experiences/ prefix. No AggregateRating, Offer prices, HowTo or TouristTrip.
sections: 1. intro-section. Label 'Why Charter'. First h2, e.g. 'The Whole Boat, Not a Cabin on It'. p.answer-capsule, then three intro-body paragraphs: (a) what a crewed charter is: you hire the vessel and its crew for a fixed term, usually a week, and the itinerary is agreed with the captain each morning within weather and cruising-ground limits; (b) who it is for: families and groups of friends filling every cabin, multigenerational trips (link /experiences/multigenerational-travel/), and celebrations (link /experiences/romance-celebration-travel/); (c) WHO IT IS NOT FOR, which NEW-CONTENT-PROMPT requires: a couple travelling alone, where the per-cabin economics favour a small ship (link /experiences/cruises/mediterranean/ once it exists, otherwise /experiences/cruises/), travellers who need a fixed daily port schedule, and anyone with severe motion sickness (this extends parent FAQ 5 and does not repeat it). The intro-image is a portrait np-/ni- crop that differs from the hero; see images.

2. inclusions-section, used for the three boat types: 'Gulet, Catamaran or Motor Yacht' (h2). Three to four inclusion-items: Gulet (wooden motor-sailer from Turkey's Aegean and Mediterranean coast, a cabin count drawn from the gulet's own spec sheet, motors more than it sails, deck space for groups); Sailing or power catamaran (Greek islands and the Caribbean, stable at anchor, shallow draft for beach anchorages); Motor yacht (speed between islands, more range per day, higher fuel spend inside the APA); and optionally Crew (captain, chef, deckhand or stewardess, and what each does). Do not place a cabin, guest or crew number without a source, because charter guest limits vary by flag and by vessel (see sources).

3. exp-cards-section id="destinations" (the standard experience id; also the target of the hero secondary CTA if it is switched). h2 e.g. 'Where We Charter'. exp-cards exp-cards--photo with six cards, each an <a class="exp-card"> to a destination page and never to /plan-your-trip/, with no <a> nested inside: Greek islands → /destinations/greece/#places; the Amalfi coast and the Italian islands → /destinations/italy/#places; French Riviera → /destinations/france/#places; Antigua and the Eastern Caribbean → /destinations/barbados-eastern-caribbean/#places; St. Barth's → /destinations/st-barths/; the Lau Group in Fiji → /destinations/fiji/#places. Turkey has no destination page, so it lives in section 4 (#gulets) and gets no card. Croatia also has no page; mention it only in body copy.

4. events-section 'Trips We Plan Often' (h2). Three or four event-cards; every event-cta goes to /plan-your-trip/, which is the allowed event exception. Card 1 is <div class="event-card" id="gulets">, 'A Gulet of Your Own': 7 days, Turkey's Turquoise Coast, a Bodrum–Göcek or Fethiye routing, ruins by tender. Its event-when carries the reconciled season (NEEDS MARK). The id names this card in the 'Trips We Plan Often' events-section. It answers event-card 4 on its own and has at least two consumers (the parent event-card 4 secondary link, the romance page, and two journal posts). Card 2: Greek islands by crewed catamaran (Cyclades or Ionian, plus the July–August meltemi caveat). Card 3: a Caribbean motor yacht week (Antigua base, cross-linked in body to the Barbados & Eastern Caribbean 'The Sailing Version' itinerary rather than restating it). Optional card 4: Lau Group private charter of 7–10 days (summarised from /destinations/fiji/ with a link, not duplicated).

5. A second inclusions-section, 'What We Handle on a Charter' (h2). This goes one level deeper than the parent's 'Charter Brokerage' item. Items: the broker and the vessel shortlist (association-member brokers, with sources); crew references and the pre-charter preference sheet; the contract (MYBA terms in the Med, and what the deposit and balance schedule says); the APA (how it is held, what it covers, accounting and refund at disembarkation); embarkation logistics (flights timed to a Saturday handover, marina transfers); and gratuity guidance, given as a sourced norm or left out.

6. seasons-strip 'Charter Season by Ground' (h2). season-items: Eastern Mediterranean and Greece (with the meltemi caveat, sourced to HNMS); Turkey's gulet season (NEEDS MARK reconciliation, see below); the Caribbean (December–April, outside NOAA's 1 June–30 November Atlantic hurricane season), carrying season-item--best only if Mark confirms; the Fiji/Lau dry season of May–October, taken from /destinations/fiji/.

7. exp-cta. h2 e.g. 'Plan a Charter Worth the Week'. Body asks for the coastline, the dates, the group size and the cabin split. Buttons: Plan My Charter → /plan-your-trip/ and a ghost link back to /experiences/cruises/ ('All cruise styles'), not to /experiences/.

8. cost-range as a noBand row. A new key in tools/cost-ranges-data.mjs for the new content file, with unit e.g. 'Priced per vessel per week, not per person' and no currency amount. Includes: the boat, its crew, and the standard toys and fuel at a basic cruising allowance where the contract states it. Excludes: the APA (food, drink, fuel, berthing, which is drawn down and reconciled), VAT where it applies, crew gratuity, flights. Drivers must carry at least one checkable number: the APA percentage (from MYBA/CYBA/IYBA guidance), a country charter-VAT rate (from the Greek/Italian/Croatian tax authority), or NOAA hurricane dates. The source is a broker-association or tax-authority URL. No per-person band.
9. page-faq with 8 questions using the pf-q/pf-a markup and ids pf-yacht-charters-1…8. Each answer opens with a complete answer in 25 words or fewer.

10. read-more ('From the Journal'). Three cards: /travel-journal/mediterranean-october/ (Croatia and Turkey, the last gulet month), /travel-journal/middle-east-destination-guide/ (Turkey and the Turquoise Coast gulet season), /travel-journal/caribbean-mexico-destination-guide/ (charter operator to the cays). This meets the floor of at least two journal links.
briefs.answerCapsuleDirection: Put 40–70 words under the first h2 that answer the question 'how does a private crewed charter work?' The capsule should say four things. (1) You hire the whole vessel and its crew, usually for a week. The Saturday-to-Saturday norm comes from MYBA/charter-broker association guidance. (2) The charter fee is the base, and on top of it you pay an APA deposit of a stated percentage, drawn down for fuel, food, drinks and berthing, with the balance reconciled and returned. The percentage must come from MYBA, CYBA or IYBA published guidance and must not be invented; if no published figure is found, say 'a percentage set in the contract' and drop the number. (3) Gulets, catamarans and motor yachts suit different grounds. (4) The seasons: the Caribbean runs outside NOAA's 1 June–30 November Atlantic hurricane season (nhc.noaa.gov), and the Mediterranean window comes from the parent page's May–October framing, cross-checked against the gulet NEEDS MARK. The NOAA dates are the guaranteed number. No first-person experience claims go in the capsule.

briefs.primaryIntent: Commercial investigation. The visitor has already decided on a river cruise in Europe and wants to know which river (Rhine, Danube, Rhône or Douro) and which kind of ship fits them. They also want to know where the ships really dock (Vienna, Budapest, Lyon) and when to sail, with April and October as the shoulder months and low-water risk in late summer. Secondary: the Lyon–Avignon Rhône wine trip promised by the parent's event-card 3, deep-linked at #rhone.

briefs.h1Direction:

briefs.answerCapsuleDirection: Place it directly under the first h2 (intro-title), 40–70 words, answering 'which river and when' in one pass. It should pair each river with its strength: Rhine for castles and the UNESCO Upper Middle Rhine gorge, Danube for Vienna and Budapest, Rhône for Lyon-to-Avignon wine country, Douro for terraced vineyards and high locks. Then state the typical length and the shoulder months. Allowed numbers, each tied to its source: (a) the Upper Middle Rhine Valley's 65 km length from UNESCO WHC list entry 1066; (b) a typical sailing of 7 nights, from at least two lines' published itinerary pages (Viking, AmaWaterways, Scenic, Uniworld or Avalon), stated as 'typically'; (c) the Carrapatelo lock lift on the Douro (about 35 m) from APDL (Douro waterway authority) only if verified there; (d) April and October as shoulder months, matching the parent tile and the seasons strip. Never invent passenger counts, ship dimensions, prices or 'most popular' rankings. If a figure cannot be sourced, cut it.

The huts open from [opening month] to [closing month] (one window, cited to CAI or the provincial tourism board: Dolomiti/Südtirol, Veneto/Provincia di Belluno, Trentino). Do not reuse 'six days' or 'July-September' from the existing event-card without checking. Do not invent a price.

briefs.answerCapsuleDirection:
Write it under the intro-section h2, in 40–70 words. It should answer "how do I plan a culture trip to Oaxaca and Mexico City" in one self-contained block: the best window, how to split the trip, and the timing traps.
- Best window: October to April. Source: SMN/CONAGUA climate normals for Oaxaca and CDMX.
- Trip length and split: for example "8–10 days, 4–5 nights in Oaxaca". This is an HYMT planning claim, so it needs the owner's confirmation before it ships.
- Flight time: the CDMX–Oaxaca hop of about one hour. Source: the Aeroméxico or Viva published schedule, with the date checked. Never estimate it.
- Timing traps: Día de Muertos runs October 31 to November 2 (source: UNESCO ICH listing 00054 or the Mexican government's cultura.gob.mx), and the Museo Nacional de Antropología closes on Mondays (source: mna.inah.gob.mx).
Use at least one of these numbers. No invented figures, and no superlative unless it is attributed.
faqCandidates: How many days do I need for Oaxaca and Mexico City? (first sentence a complete answer; split owner-confirmed)
Should I start in Mexico City or Oaxaca? (altitude ~2,240 m in CDMX vs ~1,550 m Oaxaca per INEGI; flight connection)
When is the best time to visit Oaxaca? (dry season Oct-Apr per SMN; festival trade-offs)
How far ahead should I book Oaxaca for Día de Muertos? (Oct 31-Nov 2; lead time is NEEDS MARK)
Is Oaxaca safe for travelers? (cite US State Dept Mexico travel advisory by state, dated; Oaxaca and CDMX levels as published that day)
How do I get from Mexico City to Oaxaca - fly or drive? (flight ~1 hr vs ~6-7 hr by road via ADO/highway 150D; cite carriers/SCT)
Do I need tickets in advance for Frida Kahlo's Casa Azul? (yes, timed online tickets per museofridakahlo.org.mx)
Is the Anthropology Museum worth a full day, and what day is it closed? (closed Mondays per INAH/MNA)
Can you visit Monte Albán and Mitla in one day? (distances/hours per INAH)
Is a mezcal palenque visit suitable if I don't drink? (what a palenque visit involves; NEEDS MARK on the producers used)

UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage: Indigenous festivity dedicated to the dead (00054); Traditional Mexican cuisine (00400)

INAH (inah.gob.mx) for site hours, closures and admission fees at Monte Albán, Mitla, Templo Mayor and Teotihuacan, and the Museo Nacional de Antropología (mna.inah.gob.mx) for its Monday closure and hours
Museo Frida Kahlo / Casa Azul (museofridakahlo.org.mx) for timed tickets and the Anahuacalli combined ticket
Consejo Regulador del Mezcal (CRM) and the NOM-070-SCFI-2016 mezcal standard for the categories ancestral, artesanal and mezcal, and the Denominación de Origen states
Oaxaca state government / Secretaría de Turismo de Oaxaca for the Guelaguetza dates (the Mondays after July 16), checked for the current year
SMN/CONAGUA climatological normals for Oaxaca and Mexico City (the dry and rainy season months)
INEGI for the elevations of Mexico City (~2,240 m) and Oaxaca de Juárez
US Department of State, Mexico Travel Advisory (state-by-state levels), dated on the page
SAT, Ley del IVA Article 1 (16% IVA), the same source the riviera-maya-los-cabos cost block already uses; Oaxaca and CDMX lodging-tax (ISH) rates from the state finance ministries
Aeroméxico and Viva published schedules for the MEX–OAX flight time

briefs.answerCapsuleDirection:
The capsule answers "What is a Namibia trip and how do you plan it?" in 40–70 words, directly under the intro h2. Name the four anchor regions (Sossusvlei, Damaraland, Skeleton Coast, Etosha), the best window, and the fly-in vs self-drive trade-off. Use at least one number, each from a named source, never invented:
- Etosha's size (about 22,270 km²) from MEFT / Namibia Wildlife Resorts.
- Sossusvlei's dune heights, or the Namib Sand Sea's World Heritage inscription and area, from UNESCO WHC (site 1430).
- Namibia's population density, among the lowest on earth, from the Namibia Statistics Agency or the World Bank.
- The Windhoek–Sossusvlei–Etosha road distance from the Roads Authority or a mapped route.
- The dry-season months from the Meteorological Service of Namibia.
Link the figure used to its source inline. No first-hand claim in the capsule unless Mark confirms one.
faqCandidates: When is the best time to visit Namibia? (Dry season for Etosha vs green season; months sourced from the Meteorological Service of Namibia.)

Should we self-drive Namibia or fly between camps? (Distances, gravel roads, tyre and insurance realities; a charter leg's cost against days saved. Advisory figures from the Roads Authority / US State Dept road-safety page.)
How many days do you need in Namibia? (Circuit length by region pairing; the answer depends on fly-in vs road.)

Is Etosha as good as a Botswana or Kenya safari? (Honest comparison: waterhole concentration and a self-drive park vs private-concession density; link /destinations/botswana/ and /destinations/kenya-tanzania/.)
Can you combine Namibia with Botswana and Victoria Falls? (Routing via the Zambezi Region/Kasane; link /destinations/zambia-victoria-falls/.)
Is Namibia malaria-free? (Coast and Sossusvlei vs northern Etosha/Zambezi Region; cite CDC Yellow Book / Namibia Ministry of Health.)

Do US citizens need a visa for Namibia? (Namibia moved to visa requirements for US citizens in 2025. Verify current e-visa/visa-on-arrival rules with Namibia's Ministry of Home Affairs and travel.state.gov, show a 'verified as of' date, and add a verify-before-travel line.)
Is Namibia good for families with children? (Malaria-light southern circuit, minimum ages at lodges and on activities NEEDS MARK, long transfers.)
What does a luxury Namibia trip cost? (Range from the cost-range block, dated; NEEDS FIGURE.)
Where can you see desert-adapted elephant and black rhino? (Damaraland/Kunene, with the conservancy model credited to Save the Rhino Trust Namibia / NACSO.)

briefs.primaryIntent: A West Coast family planning a Disneyland long weekend. They want to know how many days both parks need, how date-based tickets and park reservations lock the calendar, whether to stay at one of the three Disney hotels or off-site, why Disneyland is the stronger Disney resort for children under six, and which Orange County beach town to add. Search shape: "Disneyland trip planning", "Disneyland with toddlers", "how many days at Disneyland", "Disneyland long weekend", "Disneyland vs Disney World" (shared with Orlando, so handled by one comparison FAQ).
briefs.workingTitle: Disneyland & the Orange County Coast — Hit Your Mark Travel
briefs.h1Direction:
The H1 is hero.headline (DestinationLayout renders it as h1.dest-hero__headline). Use a 2-3 line claim in the house voice, built on the page's thesis and not a superlative. Direction: the original Disney park is the compact one, sized for a long weekend and for small children. Example shape only: "The Original Disney Park
Is the One Built
for Small Children." It must not repeat the title verbatim. hero.sub (about 60-80 words) carries the specifics: two parks on one esplanade, Disney's own "at least three days" advice, and date-based tickets plus park reservation. Primary CTA "Plan a Disneyland Trip" -> /plan-your-trip/. Secondary "Explore the Parks ↓" -> #places.
briefs.metaDescription: Disney advises at least three days for Disneyland's two Anaheim parks. Park reservations, the three Disney hotels, and why it is the stronger pick for under-sixes.
briefs.breadcrumb: Home > Destinations > North America > Disneyland & Orange County. The layout builds it from region + name. BreadcrumbList follows the same trail array automatically. It cannot vary by referrer, so a family-travel visitor returns via the body link and FAQ link to /experiences/family-travel/ (and the FeaturedIn strip once phase B ships).
briefs.schemaNodes: DestinationLayout's set, unchanged: WebPage + BreadcrumbList (4 items, matching the visible trail) + TouristDestination (name "Disneyland & Orange County", nominative use of the Disney name only; containedInPlace per the layout's region handling) + FAQPage built from the page-faq block. Do not add: AggregateRating, Event or Product nodes for parks or tickets, an Organization node for Disney, logos, or HowTo. Canonical, og and twitter tags are inherited from Base.astro. og:image comes from a new og-anaheim-disneyland-pier-golden-hour.jpg entry in src/lib/og-crops.ts, generated by tools/make-og-crops.mjs and never hand-edited. Until that exists, it falls back to /assets/og-default.jpg.
sections: 1. section.intro-section: label 'Why Disneyland'; h2.intro-title (first h2, a thesis line along the lines of 'Smaller Than Orlando. That Is the Point.'); p.answer-capsule (40-70 words, see capsule direction); 2-3 p.intro-body covering the long-weekend logic, the under-six argument and the dates-before-flights order of operations; div.intro-image.intro-image--photo holding an np- portrait (GAP) with an intro-image-label caption. Link /experiences/family-travel/ here with anchor text such as 'how we plan family trips by age'.

2. section.places-section id="places": h2 such as 'Six Pieces of a Disneyland Trip Worth Planning Properly'. Six a.place-card, each a full anchor with no nested <a>, using place-card__img/__body/__region/__name/__desc/__tags/place-tag/__arrow. Cards: (a) Disneyland Park [Anaheim]; (b) Disney California Adventure [Anaheim]; (c) The Disney Hotels & Downtown Disney [Anaheim], covering the three hotels and the early-entry and walkability question, with benefits taken from Disney's hotel pages; (d) Newport Beach & Balboa [Orange County Coast]; (e) Laguna Beach & Dana Point [Orange County Coast]; (f) San Diego & La Jolla add-on [San Diego County]. Card hrefs: (a)-(c) point to /plan-your-trip/, or to a sourced external authority only if the house pattern allows it. (d)-(f) also go to /plan-your-trip/, since no on-site page exists. Never point a card at another HYMT page that does not cover the place. Drop Los Angeles (proposed in the audit) so the page stays honest to its 'Orange County Coast' name. Every card needs a real photo, or the grid must not use the --photo class.

3. section.itineraries-section 'Trips We Plan Often': four .itin-card (itin-image itin-image--photo with an ni- 3:4 portrait, itin-body, itin-duration, itin-name, itin-meta, itin-desc, itin-cta). Proposed: 'Three Days, Two Parks' (3 days); 'The West Coast Long Weekend' (Thu-Sun, framed around date-based tickets); 'Disneyland With Under-Sixes' (4 days, height-minimum-free attractions, midday hotel break); 'Disneyland and the Coast' (5-6 days, parks then Laguna or Newport). Durations and pacing are HYMT planning advice. Any first-hand claim gets a NEEDS MARK.

4. section.why-section 'What We Add to Disneyland Planning': four .why-item (why-icon, why-title, why-desc). Cover: locking ticket dates and park reservations before flights; hotel choice by walking distance against budget; the under-six day shape; and Lightning Lane and dining windows, with rules taken from Disney's pages and dated. No claim of a Disney advisor credential unless Mark supplies one.

5. section.seasons-strip 'Disneyland by Season': .seasons-grid with three .season-item, one .season-item--best carrying a .season-badge. Windows to source: lower-demand periods (January to early March, September, early November, from Disney's ticket-tier calendar), summer and holiday peaks, and the Halloween and holiday seasonal overlays (dates from Disneyland's events pages). 'June gloom' marine-layer weather should be attributed to NOAA/NWS Los Angeles. Show the verification date on the page.

6. section.dest-cta: h2.dest-cta__title ('Plan a Disneyland Trip
Sized for the Kids You Have' or similar); dest-cta__body asking for children's ages, dates and the home airport; btn-primary-gold to /plan-your-trip/; btn-ghost-gold to /destinations/north-america/ ('All North America'); dest-cta__note kept as the house line.

7. section.related-section data-p3-6 'Destinations Worth Comparing': three related-card entries generated by tools/p3-6-related-destinations.mjs or hand-placed to the same shape. Use /destinations/orlando/ (only once it exists), /destinations/hawaii/ (the West Coast family alternative, already on the family-travel page) and /destinations/napa-sonoma/ (California, the adult counterpart). related-more links to /destinations/north-america/. Related cards use alt="" aria-hidden="true" rc- crops.

8. section.cost-range 'What Disneyland Actually Costs': inserted via a COST_RANGES entry in tools/p3-8-cost-insert.mjs. State the basis (per family of four per day, or per person per night, matching sibling pages), what is included, what moves the figure (ticket tier by date, Park Hopper, Lightning Lane, Disney hotel vs off-site), and a dated 'verified' line. Every figure needs a NEEDS FIGURE until it is sourced from Disneyland's ticket and hotel pricing on a stated date.

9. section.page-faq: 6-10 .pf-item with ids pf-disneyland-1..n, h3.pf-q-h > button.pf-q with aria-expanded and aria-controls, and div.pf-a with role=region. The first sentence of each answer is a complete answer in 25 words or fewer. Link the Orlando comparison answer to /destinations/orlando/, and one answer to /experiences/family-travel/.

10. section.read-more 'Read More on Disneyland': at least 2 (prefer 3) .read-more__card links to journal posts: /travel-journal/north-america-destination-guide/, /travel-journal/the-case-for-shoulder-season/ (crowd windows), /travel-journal/in-defense-of-slow-travel/ (the pacing argument). Alternate: /travel-journal/what-a-travel-advisor-actually-does/.
briefs.answerCapsuleDirection: Place p.answer-capsule directly under the first h2 (intro-title), at 40-70 words. Answer directly how long a Disneyland trip needs and who it suits best. Required numbers, each from a named source and never estimated: (1) 'at least three days' for both parks, from Disneyland's own trip-length page, https://disneyland.disney.go.com/destinations/visit/, which family-travel already cites; (2) the count of attractions with no height requirement ('more than 60' as the family-travel tile states), recounted from Disneyland's official height-requirements listing on the build date and dated on the page; (3) optionally, 'two parks' and 'three Disney hotels' from Disneyland's parks and hotels pages. Shape: two parks on one esplanade in Anaheim, three days per Disney, a long weekend for West Coast families, and the stronger Disney resort for under-sixes because of the no-minimum attraction count. Close with the order of operations: lock dated tickets and the park reservation before the flights. Do not compare drive times or crowd levels with numbers unless they are sourced.
faqCandidates: How many days do you need at Disneyland? (Disney advises at least three for both parks; source: Disneyland visit page.)

Is Disneyland or Walt Disney World better for young children? (Comparison FAQ: answer for under-sixes, then link /destinations/orlando/ for the full Orlando case; the Orlando page carries the mirror FAQ linking back.)
Do I need a park reservation as well as a ticket? (Source: Disneyland's ticket and park-reservation pages; date the answer.)
Is it worth staying at a Disney hotel at Disneyland? (Walking distance, any hotel-guest entry benefit, cost against Anaheim off-site; benefits from Disney's hotel pages only.)
What is the best time of year to visit Disneyland? (Ticket-tier calendar low-demand windows; Halloween and holiday overlay dates.)
Can you do Disneyland as a long weekend? (Yes for West Coast families; a 3-day shape plus travel days.)
How many Disneyland rides have no height requirement? (Count from the official height-requirements list, with the date.)
Is Park Hopper worth it at Disneyland? (Answer from the parks' layout plus Disney's Park Hopper rules; no invented time savings.)
Which beach town should we add after Disneyland? (Newport/Balboa vs Laguna/Dana Point vs San Diego; distances only from a cited source such as Google Maps or Caltrans, otherwise left out.)
When should we book a Disneyland trip? (Ticket and reservation availability, hotel booking windows per Disney; HYMT lead-time advice flagged NEEDS MARK if experience-based.)

briefs.primaryIntent: A US traveler choosing a high-end Southwest trip, who wants to know which base (Tucson destination spa, Sedona, or southern Utah canyon country), when to go, and how to combine them. Destination-spa programs (Canyon Ranch Tucson, Miraval Arizona) are the wellness angle, red rock and the national parks are the landscape angle. This page is the canonical target for wellness-retreat-travel exp-card 5 ("Arizona & Southwest"), which currently points at /plan-your-trip/. Intent is distinct from /experiences/wellness-retreat-travel/ (a global comparison of six wellness regions), from /travel-journal/north-america-destination-guide/ (a continent overview with one Southwest card) and from /destinations/aspen/ (Colorado Rockies ski). CONDITIONAL: build only if the owner confirms the practice books the Southwest often enough to stand behind a full guide and an "itineraries we plan" section. If he declines, the tile resolves to /travel-journal/north-america-destination-guide/ (the Southwest card has no stable id; ask for id="american-southwest" on that island-card) or stays an explicit exception in tile-map.json.
briefs.workingTitle: American Southwest | Sedona, Utah & Spas — Hit Your Mark Travel
briefs.h1Direction:
The H1 comes from the hero headline in the wrapper (DestinationLayout renders it), using the 2-3 line
pattern of Turks & Caicos. Direction: a specific claim that the Southwest is three different trips (a spa week in Tucson, red rock in Sedona, Utah's canyon parks) and the planning work is choosing and sequencing them. No superlative without a source. Exactly one h1. The body opens at h2.
briefs.metaDescription: Sedona red rock, Utah's five national parks and destination-spa weeks at Canyon Ranch and Miraval in Tucson, planned for the October-to-April window.
briefs.breadcrumb: Home > Destinations > North America > American Southwest (built by DestinationLayout from the region prop; the BreadcrumbList JSON-LD renders from the same trail)
briefs.schemaNodes: WebPage + BreadcrumbList (4 items, matching the visible trail) + TouristDestination (name "American Southwest", containedInPlace North America hub; touristType wellness and outdoor travelers; includesAttraction only for places named in the place-cards) + FAQPage (from the page-faq block, 6-10 Q&As). All are emitted by DestinationLayout per SCHEMA-LIBRARY.md § 4. No AggregateRating, no HowTo, no SearchAction. Brand names (Canyon Ranch, Miraval, Amangiri) appear as text only, never as Hotel/LodgingBusiness nodes the site cannot vouch for.

Then intro-body paragraphs: three trips, not one; who each suits; the October-April heat logic. Link to /experiences/wellness-retreat-travel/ and /destinations/north-america/ in body copy with descriptive anchors.

2. places-section id="places" (required stable anchor; the hero's secondary CTA targets it): h2 plus intro, then a place-card grid of 6 cards (.place-card is an anchor, so no nested <a>). Each card carries __img, __region, __name, __desc and place-tags. Candidates: Tucson destination spas (Canyon Ranch, Miraval) [Southern Arizona]; Sedona and Verde Valley [Northern Arizona]; Zion and Bryce Canyon [Southwestern Utah]; Arches, Canyonlands and Moab [Southeastern Utah]; Lake Powell and Canyon Point (Amangiri, Antelope Canyon via Navajo-permitted tours) [Utah-Arizona border]; Grand Canyon South/North Rim [Northern Arizona]. The cards have no internal destination pages to link to, so each card's href should be #itineraries-style in-page only if a stable id exists. Better: render them as non-linking cards if the template allows, or link each card to its official NPS page. Decide in build (check how place-card hrefs are validated). With a --photo grid, every card needs a real photo; see the image gaps.

3. itineraries-section ('Trips We Plan Often'): 3-4 itin-cards with the itin-image--photo variant (ni- tiles). Candidates: 5-7 night Canyon Ranch or Miraval program week; Sedona 4 nights plus Tucson spa 4 nights; Utah Mighty 5 loop of 7-10 days from LAS (the journal's own figure); Amangiri plus Lake Powell plus Zion. itin-duration/itin-meta/itin-cta use the Turks & Caicos classes. NEEDS MARK on whether HYMT actually plans each.

briefs.answerCapsuleDirection: 40-70 words under the first h2, answering "When and how should I plan a luxury Southwest trip?" Direct answer: go October to April, pick a base by purpose (Tucson spa week, Sedona red rock, Utah canyon parks), and do not try all three in under 10 days. Allowed numbers and their required sources: "five national parks in Utah" (NPS / Utah Office of Tourism 'Mighty 5'); "7-10 day loop connects them" (already stated in /travel-journal/north-america-destination-guide/, but re-verify against NPS drive distances); Canyon Ranch or Miraval minimum stay or package length (canyonranch.com/offers, miravalresorts.com); summer average high in Phoenix or Tucson or on a canyon floor (NWS climate normals or NPS Zion weather page). Use at least one; never round or estimate.
faqCandidates: When is the best time to visit the American Southwest? (NPS park weather pages; NWS normals)
Canyon Ranch or Miraval: which destination spa suits which traveler? (official program pages; NEEDS MARK for the judgment)
How many nights does a destination-spa week need, and what is included in the package? (Canyon Ranch / Miraval package terms)
Do I need reservations or timed-entry permits for Zion, Arches or the Grand Canyon? (nps.gov current reservation rules, dated)
Can I combine Sedona, Tucson and Utah's national parks in one trip, and how long does it take? (drive times, Google/ADOT/UDOT; 7-10 days for Utah parks alone)
Which airport should I fly into: Phoenix, Tucson, Las Vegas or Salt Lake City? (gateway fact already on the NA journal guide; airline-neutral)
How far ahead should I book Amangiri or Enchantment Resort for spring and fall? (journal says Amangiri 12+ months; NEEDS MARK to confirm)
Is the Southwest too hot in summer, and what about the monsoon? (NWS Phoenix/Tucson monsoon season Jun 15-Sep 30)
Is the Southwest good for a first family national-parks trip? (only if Mark confirms; else drop)
Do I need a guide for Antelope Canyon or the slot canyons? (Navajo Nation Parks & Recreation: Antelope Canyon by tour only)
